annotation.kind: source-faithful finite-matrix formalization of the componentwise part of Lemma 2.1

assumptions: The rows and columns are indexed by Fin n in their natural order.
The hypothesis on D is the componentwise condition |D| <= delta I; in particular it forces every off-diagonal entry of D to be zero.
The predicate p36StrictUpper says that N_ij is zero whenever j <= i.
Complex entrywise absolute values are represented by nonnegative real norms, and the truncated upper limit min(k,n-1) is represented by zeroing terms with r >= n inside the range 0 through k.

conditions.L: The identical fixed statement and P36 shared files are present; the frozen NumStability library is also present.
conditions.N: The fixed statement and P36 shared files are present; no NumStability artifact is present.

formal_statement.lean_header: theorem p36_t3_truncated_binomial_power_bound (n k D N delta) (hD) (hN) : forall i j, |(D+N)^k|_ij <= sum_{r=0}^{min(k,n-1)} choose(k,r) delta^(k-r) (|N|^r)_ij
formal_statement.plain_language: Every entry of the absolute value of a power of a bounded diagonal matrix plus a strictly upper-triangular matrix is bounded by the paper's truncated binomial majorant.

informal_proof: Bound the absolute value of a complex matrix product by the product of the entrywise absolute-value matrices. Induct on k to dominate |(D+N)^k| by (delta I+|N|)^k. A separate band-growth induction shows that |N|^r is zero for r at least n. Since |N| commutes with delta I, expand the dominating power by the binomial theorem and delete the nilpotent tail.
informal_statement: Lemma 2.1: prove the componentwise truncated-binomial bound for powers of a diagonal matrix plus a strictly upper-triangular matrix.

paper_source.local_path: paper_bencmark/reference_papers/P36-A Schur-Parlett Algorithm for Computing Matrix Functions.pdf

paper_version: published journal version; SIAM Journal on Matrix Analysis and Applications 25(2), 2003, printed pages 464-485

patterns: diagonal plus strictly upper triangular power bound
absence_search.result: Neither Mathlib nor the importable frozen NumStability set contains Lemma 2.1, its componentwise diagonal-plus-strict-upper power majorant, or a theorem that supplies the required band nilpotence and truncated expansion. Related Jordan, matrix-power, and Sylvester developments in the frozen repository are not part of the compiled condition-L bundle.
absence_search.scope: the complete frozen NumStability source, the compiled condition-L bundle recorded in metadata/library_olean.json, and Mathlib

review_record_not_for_run_prompt.note: The private N and L proofs reconstruct the same entrywise product estimate, nonnegative matrix monotonicity, strict-upper band induction, nilpotent-tail removal, and commuting matrix binomial expansion. L uses only an irrelevant zero-nonnegativity marker and receives no material shortcut. The formal upper limit follows the displayed statement of Lemma 2.1; it does not reproduce the evident n-1 versus n indexing typo in one sentence of the paper's proof.

source_locations.role: selected componentwise power-bound statement and proof
source_locations.section: 2. Evaluating functions of the atomic blocks

tier_rationale: The proof must establish entrywise absolute-value domination for complex matrix multiplication, monotonicity of nonnegative matrix products, a dimension-indexed band theorem and nilpotence result for strict upper triangular matrices, and a commuting matrix binomial expansion with exact truncation. This is substantial multi-stage formalization work and is not discharged by Mathlib imports. NumStability has no corresponding compiled theorem, so L receives no material advantage over N.
